title: Pocketwire Advance Largest Available Advance
content:
When a customer asks for the largest advance their Pocketwire Advance line can take, the customer requests that amount in the app as a standard delivery to an external debit card. The flat advance fee and the due date of that advance are those the Pocketwire Advance fee rules and disbursement rules set, and they are booked with it.

## Standing conditions

The largest advance a line can take is worked out only after every late fee on the line that qualifies for payroll-delay relief carries its relief waiver entry. While any such late fee is without its relief waiver entry, the largest advance of the line is not yet worked out.

The largest advance worked out for the line takes the place of the effective limit as the ceiling on a new advance: a new advance may not exceed it, and the remaining principal of the line's advances is already taken off in it.

The amount of a new advance is at least the tier's smallest advance, a whole multiple of the tier's advance increment and within the largest advance worked out for the line, and the count of advances not yet fully repaid together with the new one still may not exceed the tier's number of advances outstanding at once.

## Bounds on the amount requested

| Bound | Rule |
|---|---|
| Ceiling | The largest advance worked out for the line |
| Floor | The tier's smallest advance |
| Steps | A whole multiple of the tier's advance increment |
| Count | Advances not yet fully repaid, together with the new one, within the tier's number outstanding at once |
| Delivery | Standard delivery to an external debit card |

## Requesting the advance: `request_advance_00c9f515`

**Capability.** The customer requests a new advance on their Pocketwire Advance line, delivered by standard delivery to their external debit card. One call books the advance with today's date and the current moment as its disbursement time, the due date given, and its flat advance fee for the amount given; the amount the customer owes on the line goes up by the advance plus that fee. The customer sees the new advance, its reference, its fee and its due date in the app at once. The tool does not check eligibility or timing and does not compute the amounts it is handed.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool`, which hands it to the customer, and the customer themselves runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`, using the tool name `request_advance_00c9f515` and the argument values the agent gives.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `advance_line_id` | The reference number of the customer's advance line, as returned by the advance line lookup (`find_advance_lines`) | Identifier |
| `amount` | The advance principal in USD | 2 decimal places, a whole multiple of the tier's advance increment; stored exactly as given |
| `due_date` | The repayment due date of the new advance | A calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD (Eastern Time) |
| `flat_fee` | The flat advance fee in USD | 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent before it is passed; stored exactly as given |

**Return.** A text rendering of a dictionary confirming the advance: `advance_entry_id` (reference number of the advance), `advance_reference` (the advance reference shown in the app), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places), `flat_fee` (USD, 2 decimal places), `fee_entry_id` (reference number of the fee entry), `due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `delivery` (always standard delivery to the external debit card) and `outstanding_balance` (USD, 2 decimal places, what the customer owes on the line afterwards). A returned `advance_reference` means the advance is booked.
